Running a 3B parameter model on a mobile device sounds impressive until your app crashes from an Out Of Memory error on mid-tier hardware.

Most mobile teams fail at on-device AI because they treat edge inference like server-side API calls.

Shrinking a model to INT4 quantization is only half the battle. If your runtime leaks native memory or stalls the main thread during tensor allocation, the user experience collapses.

⚡ Memory allocation patterns: Server runtimes allocate memory fluidly on demand. On mobile, unmanaged heap allocation triggers thermal throttling and aggressive kills by the OS low-memory daemon.

🛠️ Engine overhead: Heavy runtimes bloat your binary size before loading a single weight file into memory. Frameworks like ExecuTorch isolate execution graphs to keep the native footprint minimal.

📌 Thread context switching: Routing tensor execution to the NPU or GPU requires strict memory mapping. Default background thread pools still fight with UI rendering pipelines for cache locality.

Prioritize static memory allocation profiles and hardware delegate stability before optimizing raw token generation speed. A reliable 12 tokens per second beats a choppy 30 tokens per second that crashes mid-session.

Are you targeting GPU/NPU delegates for your local models, or sticking to CPU execution for broader device coverage?
